statement: Build a single-file website for Paws Haven animal shelter in Mysuru with pets for adoption, donate, volunteer sign-up, success stories, and a full English/Kannada version.
audience: Prospective adopters, donors and volunteers in and around Mysuru, reading English or Kannada, mostly on mobile phones.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file, CDN libraries allowed, no build step.
Mobile-first responsive layout that stays readable at 360px width.
Accessible basics: alt text on images, labels on form fields, readable contrast, keyboard-usable navigation and toggle.
Kannada text renders with a Kannada-capable font and does not overflow or break layouts.
No personal data is stored, and none is sent to a third-party service.
rules: Donate takes no payment on the site: show UPI QR and bank details only, with no gateway, card form or payment script.
Adoption inquiries and volunteer sign-ups open a pre-filled WhatsApp or email message to the shelter; there is no backend and no third-party form service.
Kannada is full parity with an English/Kannada toggle, machine-drafted and labelled as pending native-speaker review.
Invent no shelter facts. Any fact the brief does not give appears as a visibly marked placeholder.
Pet profiles and success stories that are not supplied are shown as clearly labelled sample entries, not as real animals or real adopters.
done_when: The site is one HTML file with its CSS and JavaScript inline or loaded from CDN, and needs no build step.
The file shows the name Paws Haven and Mysuru, and has navigation to Home, Adopt, Donate, Volunteer and Success Stories sections.
The Adopt section lists pets, each with name, species, age and a short description, and each has an inquiry button that opens a pre-filled WhatsApp or email message.
The Donate section shows a UPI QR area and bank details as marked placeholders, and the file contains no payment gateway script, card input or payment form.

The Volunteer section has a sign-up form with labelled fields (at least name, phone, email, availability) whose submit action opens a pre-filled WhatsApp or email message, and the file has no form action posting to an external service and no data storage code.
The Success Stories section shows at least three stories, each with a pet name and a short text.
An English/Kannada toggle is present, and every visible text string, including nav, buttons, form labels, placeholders and messages, has a Kannada version that the toggle switches to.
In Kannada mode and in English mode the file shows a visible notice that the Kannada text is pending native-speaker review.
The file loads a Kannada-capable font and sets the page lang attribute to match the selected language.
Every shelter fact not given in the brief (UPI ID, QR image, bank details, phone, WhatsApp number, email, address) appears as a visibly marked placeholder.
The file has a viewport meta tag and responsive CSS rules for narrow screens.
open_inputs: UPI ID and UPI QR code image
Native Kannada speaker to review the Kannada text
